15 A box, in the shape of a cube, falls from a ship into the sea. The box lands with its lower face
level with the surface of the sea.

The box begins to sink, becomes totally submerged and then sinks deeper into the sea.
As the box sinks, its lower face is always parallel to the surface of the sea.
Which graph best represents the variation of the upthrust acting on the box with the depth of its
lower face below the surface of the sea?

hints: Notice the x-axis is the depth of the lower face below the surface, starting at $0$ when the lower face is level with the sea and no water is yet displaced.
Recall Archimedes principle for upthrust: $U$ equals the weight of displaced sea water, so $U = \rho g V_{submerged}$.
Compare how $V_{submerged}$ grows while the top of the cube is still above water with what happens to $V_{submerged}$ after the top goes below the surface.
walkthrough: At depth $= 0$ the lower face just touches the sea, so displaced volume is zero and upthrust is zero. The graph must start at the origin.
By Archimedes principle, upthrust equals weight of displaced water: $U = \rho g V_{submerged}$, where $\rho$ is sea-water density.

While partly submerged, with lower face at depth $d$ and face area $A$, the submerged volume is $V_{submerged} = Ad$. So $U = \rho gAd$, which is directly proportional to $d$ and gives a straight line from the origin.
When $d$ equals the side length of the cube the box becomes totally submerged. $V_{submerged}$ then equals the full volume of the box and upthrust reaches its maximum value.
Sinking deeper does not displace more water, so $V_{submerged}$ and hence upthrust stay constant, giving a horizontal section. A linear rise from zero followed by a constant value. This is option C.

A.explanation: This shows upthrust increasing linearly for all depths, but once the cube is fully submerged the displaced volume cannot increase further.

B.explanation: This shows a large constant upthrust from zero depth, but at zero depth no water is displaced so upthrust must start at zero.

C.explanation: Upthrust rises linearly with submerged volume until the cube is just submerged, then stays constant at $U = \rho gV$ for deeper sinking.

D.explanation: This shows a curved rise, but submerged volume of the cube is $V = Ad$ so upthrust is directly proportional to depth until full submersion.
